title: Histiocytic Neoplasms
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Histiocytic Neoplasms. Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (tissue biopsy with CD1a/Langerin/S100/CD68/CD163 IHC, whole-body FDG PET-CT, brain MRI, bone marrow, and mandatory comprehensive NGS for BRAF V600E, MAP2K1, ARAF, KRAS, NRAS, CSF1R, ALK) -> Classification into Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH, adult vs pediatric, single-system bone/skin vs multisystem with or without risk organ involvement liver/spleen/hematologic) -> Erdheim-Chester Disease (ECD, hairy kidneys, symmetric long bone osteosclerosis, retro-orbital, CNS, cardiovascular) -> Rosai-Dorfman Disease (RDD, massive painless cervical lymphadenopathy, emperipolesis, extranodal skin/bone/orbit) -> Malignant Histiocytosis (Histiocytic Sarcoma) -> Targeted Therapies: Dabrafenib + Trametinib (rare-histiocytic-braf-mek) or Vemurafenib for BRAF V600E; Cobimetinib or Trametinib for MEK/MAP2K1 or BRAF-wildtype; Cladribine or Cytarabine for refractory; Corticosteroids + Vinblastine for pediatric LCH. References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Histiocytic Neoplasms Version 2.2026 (July 2026).

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Histiocytic Neoplasms: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete diagnostic workup before histologic classification. Secure tissue with definitive IHC, run mandatory molecular NGS, and stage extent of disease.
bullets: Complete history and physical examination, assessment of fever, bone pain, weight loss, neurologic/endocrine deficits (diabetes insipidus screen).
Diagnostic tissue biopsy: excisional or core biopsy of affected organ (skin, bone, lymph node, retroperitoneum).
Definitive IHC panel, LCH pattern: CD1a+, Langerin (CD207)+, S100+, CD68+ (faint); Birbeck granules on EM are historical.
Definitive IHC panel, ECD pattern: CD68+, CD163+, Factor XIIIa+, S100- (or weak/patchy), CD1a-, Langerin-. Lipid-laden foamy histiocytes with Touton giant cells and sclerosis.
Definitive IHC panel, RDD pattern: S100+ (strong), CD68+, CD163+, CD1a-, Langerin-. Hallmark emperipolesis (intact lymphocytes/erythrocytes inside histiocyte cytoplasm).
Definitive IHC panel, malignant histiocytosis / histiocytic sarcoma pattern: CD68+, CD163+, lysozyme+, high Ki-67 (>30%), cytokeratins/melanocytic/lymphoid lineage-negative.
Mandatory molecular NGS panel: high-sensitivity BRAF V600E testing (VE1 IHC plus ultra-sensitive NGS/ddPCR); broad NGS covering MAP2K1, MAP3K1, ARAF, KRAS, NRAS, PIK3CA, CSF1R, ALK fusions.

Staging and extent of disease: whole-body FDG PET-CT (skull base to mid-thigh/feet for ECD osteosclerosis); dedicated brain MRI with pituitary protocol (crucial for diabetes insipidus / infundibulum thickening in LCH and tentorial/dural thickening in ECD/RDD); echocardiogram or cardiac MRI (pericardial/atrial infiltration, aortic coating in ECD); CT abdomen/pelvis for perinephric hairy kidneys.

Laboratory baseline: CBC, CMP (hepatic/renal), coagulation profile, endocrine panel (morning cortisol, free T4, TSH, prolactin, urine osmolality with water deprivation if polyuria/polydipsia), serum/urine protein electrophoresis.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Histologic Classification

nodes.name: Histologic Classification
nodes.title: Histiocytic Neoplasms: Histologic Classification
nodes.description: Step 2: Classify the histiocytic neoplasm by histology, IHC, age group, and clinical pattern. Classification directs the disease-specific pathway.
bullets: Adult LCH: CD1a+/Langerin+ histiocytosis in an adult; stratify next by single-system versus multisystem disease and risk organ involvement.
Pediatric LCH: CD1a+/Langerin+ histiocytosis in a child; stratify next by single-system bone versus multisystem disease.

Erdheim-Chester Disease (ECD): CD68+/CD163+/Factor XIIIa+, CD1a-/Langerin- foamy histiocytosis with symmetric long bone osteosclerosis, hairy kidneys, retro-orbital, CNS, or cardiovascular involvement; stratify next by BRAF V600E status.

Rosai-Dorfman Disease (RDD): S100-strong/CD68+/CD163+ histiocytosis with emperipolesis, classically massive painless cervical lymphadenopathy with extranodal skin, bone, or orbit disease; stratify next by symptom burden.
Malignant histiocytosis / histiocytic sarcoma: high-grade CD68+/CD163+/lysozyme+ proliferation with high Ki-67 and lineage-negative markers; stratify next by resectability and systemic extent.

nodes.name: Adult LCH Extent
nodes.title: Adult LCH: Extent of Disease
nodes.description: Adult LCH confirmed. Stratify by single-system versus multisystem disease and risk organ involvement (liver, spleen, hematopoietic cytopenias).
bullets: Single-system (isolated bone or skin): unifocal or single-system disease without multisystem spread or risk organ dysfunction.
Multisystem without risk organs: disease in two or more systems but no liver, spleen, or hematopoietic (cytopenia) involvement.
Multisystem with risk organs: liver, spleen, or hematopoietic cytopenias present; risk organ involvement drives systemic and targeted therapy selection.

options.label: Multisystem with risk organs (liver, spleen, hematopoietic)

nodes.name: Pediatric LCH Extent
nodes.title: Pediatric LCH: Extent of Disease
nodes.description: Pediatric LCH confirmed. Stratify by single-system bone versus multisystem disease to select local versus frontline systemic therapy.
bullets: Single-system bone: isolated bony lesion without multisystem spread; local therapy is the standard approach.
Multisystem: disease in two or more systems (with or without risk organs); frontline systemic therapy per the LCH-IV protocol is indicated.

nodes.name: ECD BRAF Status
nodes.title: ECD: BRAF V600E Status
nodes.description: ECD confirmed. BRAF V600E is present in 50 to 65 percent of ECD and determines frontline targeted therapy.
bullets: BRAF V600E mutant (50 to 65 percent of ECD): frontline BRAF-directed therapy with profound and rapid responses in bone, cardiac, and CNS lesions.
BRAF wild-type or unknown: MEK-inhibitor or immunomodulatory/chemotherapy backbone; retest with high-sensitivity NGS/ddPCR when status is unknown.

nodes.name: RDD Symptom Burden
nodes.title: RDD: Symptom Burden and Extent
nodes.description: RDD confirmed. Stratify by asymptomatic/mild nodal disease versus symptomatic nodal or extranodal disease (skin, orbit, CNS, airway).
bullets: Asymptomatic or mild nodal: painless cervical lymphadenopathy without compressive symptoms, organ dysfunction, or progressive extranodal disease; many cases remain stable or regress.

Symptomatic nodal or extranodal (skin, orbit, CNS, airway): pain, compression, disfigurement, vision or airway compromise, neurologic deficits, or progressive disease requiring systemic therapy or surgery.

nodes.name: Malignant Histiocytosis Triage
nodes.title: Malignant Histiocytosis: Resectability and Extent
nodes.description: Malignant histiocytosis / histiocytic sarcoma confirmed. Triage by resectable localized disease versus advanced/systemic disease.
bullets: Resectable localized: solitary lesion removable with clear margins without unacceptable morbidity and no distant spread on whole-body FDG PET-CT.
Advanced or systemic: multifocal, unresectable, nodal/disseminated, or relapsed disease; test for kinase alterations (BRAF, MEK pathway, ALK) to guide conditional targeted therapy.

nodes.name: Adult LCH Single-System Treatment
nodes.title: Adult LCH, Single-System (Bone or Skin): Local Therapy
nodes.description: Isolated bone or skin LCH in an adult. Local therapy with surveillance; escalate to systemic therapy on progression or multisystem evolution.
bullets: Isolated bone lesion: curettage with or without intralesional corticosteroid; low-dose radiotherapy 10 to 20 Gy for unresectable, painful, or critical-site lesions.
Isolated skin disease: topical corticosteroids or systemic corticosteroids for limited cutaneous LCH; biopsy to confirm clearance when lesions persist.
Surveillance: clinical examination plus periodic imaging (FDG PET-CT or site-directed MRI) to detect multisystem evolution; repeat NGS if systemic therapy becomes indicated.
Escalation trigger: new lesions outside the single system, risk organ dysfunction, or BRAF V600E-positive progressive disease prompts systemic or targeted therapy.

nodes.name: Adult LCH Multisystem No-Risk-Organ Treatment
nodes.title: Adult LCH, Multisystem Without Risk Organs: Systemic Therapy
nodes.description: Multisystem adult LCH without liver, spleen, or hematopoietic involvement. Purine analogue or cytarabine backbone, with BRAF/MEK targeted therapy when BRAF V600E is present.
nodes.path: Histiocytic Neoplasms / Adult LCH / Multisystem no-risk
bullets: BRAF V600E-positive: Dabrafenib plus Trametinib per the StewardMD BRAF/MEK Standard Protocol, with dose engine calculating patient-specific doses; profound responses expected in multisystem LCH.
BRAF wild-type or unknown: cladribine monotherapy or cytarabine-based systemic therapy; confirm MAP2K1/MAPK pathway status on broad NGS because MEK inhibition is the targeted alternative.
Response assessment: whole-body FDG PET-CT with PERCIST-style metabolic response, organ function labs, and symptom review; reassess risk organ status at every restaging.
Refractory disease: switch backbone (cladribine to cytarabine or reverse) or add targeted therapy on newly identified MAPK alteration; refer for clinical trial where available.

nodes.name: Adult LCH Multisystem Risk-Organ Treatment
nodes.title: Adult LCH, Multisystem With Risk Organs: Targeted Therapy
nodes.description: Multisystem adult LCH with liver, spleen, or hematopoietic involvement. BRAF/MEK targeted therapy is preferred when BRAF V600E is present.
nodes.path: Histiocytic Neoplasms / Adult LCH / Multisystem risk-organ
bullets: BRAF V600E-positive: Dabrafenib plus Trametinib per the StewardMD BRAF/MEK Standard Protocol (preferred), with dose engine calculating patient-specific doses; monitor hepatic function and cytopenias closely given risk organ disease.
BRAF wild-type or MAP2K1-altered: cobimetinib-based MEK inhibition as the targeted alternative; high-sensitivity NGS/ddPCR confirmation of BRAF status before committing to a non-BRAF backbone.
Chemotherapy alternative: cytarabine or cladribine backbone when targeted therapy is unavailable, contraindicated, or not tolerated.
Supportive care: transfuse and correct coagulopathy for hematopoietic involvement; hepatology input for hepatic dysfunction; FDG PET-CT plus organ labs at each restaging.

nodes.name: Pediatric LCH Single-Bone Treatment
nodes.title: Pediatric LCH, Single-System Bone: Local Therapy
nodes.description: Isolated bone LCH in a child. Local therapy with function-preserving approach and surveillance for reactivation.
bullets: Curettage of the solitary bony lesion, or intralesional methylprednisolone injection for lesions where surgery risks growth-plate or joint injury.
Avoid mutilating resection and routine radiotherapy in children; reserve low-dose radiotherapy for exceptional unresectable critical-site lesions after multidisciplinary review.
Surveillance: clinical examination and site-directed imaging to confirm healing; screen for diabetes insipidus, growth disturbance, and late effects at follow-up.
Escalation trigger: new bone lesions, soft-tissue mass, or multisystem features prompts re-biopsy consideration and systemic therapy per the multisystem pathway.

nodes.name: Pediatric LCH Multisystem Treatment
nodes.title: Pediatric LCH, Multisystem: Vinblastine Plus Prednisone (LCH-IV)
nodes.description: Multisystem pediatric LCH. Frontline vinblastine plus prednisone for 12 months per the LCH-IV protocol, with targeted therapy for refractory disease.
bullets: Frontline: vinblastine plus prednisone for 12 months per the LCH-IV protocol, with dose engine calculating patient-specific weight- and surface-area-based doses.
Early response assessment at 6 to 12 weeks: poor early response predicts reactivation risk and prompts intensification per protocol strata.
Refractory or reactivated disease: cladribine or cytarabine salvage; add BRAF/MEK targeted therapy when BRAF V600E or MAPK pathway alteration is identified.
Supportive care: PJP prophylaxis during prolonged steroids, neuropathy monitoring on vinblastine, growth and endocrine surveillance, audiology where aminoglycoside exposure applies.

nodes.name: ECD BRAF-Mutant Treatment
nodes.title: ECD, BRAF V600E Mutant: BRAF-Directed Therapy (Category 1 Preferred)
nodes.description: BRAF V600E-mutant ECD. Frontline BRAF-directed therapy with profound and rapid responses in bone, cardiac, and CNS lesions.
bullets: Frontline preferred: Dabrafenib plus Trametinib per the StewardMD BRAF/MEK Standard Protocol (Category 1 preferred), with dose engine calculating patient-specific doses; expect profound and rapid responses in bone, cardiac, and CNS lesions.
Alternative BRAF-directed monotherapy: vemurafenib for BRAF V600E-positive ECD when combination therapy is not tolerated or not available.

Organ-directed monitoring: serial FDG PET-CT for osteosclerotic response, cardiac MRI or echocardiogram for pericardial/atrial and aortic disease, brain MRI for CNS/dural lesions, renal imaging for hairy kidney regression.

Long-term management: targeted therapy is continued long-term because relapse on discontinuation is common; titrate to response and tolerability with dermatologic, cardiac (LVEF), ocular (OCT), and hepatic surveillance.

nodes.name: ECD BRAF-Wildtype Treatment
nodes.title: ECD, BRAF Wild-Type or Unknown: Cobimetinib (Category 1 Preferred)
nodes.description: BRAF wild-type or unknown ECD. MEK inhibition with cobimetinib 60 mg daily is Category 1 preferred per histiocytosis approval; cladribine or tocilizumab are alternatives.
bullets: Preferred: cobimetinib 60 mg orally daily (Category 1 preferred per FDA approval for histiocytosis), with dose engine calculating patient-specific doses; assess MAP2K1 and other MAPK alterations on broad NGS.
Alternatives: cladribine purine-analogue therapy, or tocilizumab IL-6-directed therapy for inflammatory-predominant disease.
Unknown BRAF status: confirm with high-sensitivity NGS or ddPCR before excluding BRAF-directed therapy; VE1 IHC alone is insufficient to rule out V600E.
Monitoring: retinal OCT examinations, LVEF and blood pressure surveillance, CK and hepatic panels, plus FDG PET-CT and organ-directed imaging as for BRAF-mutant disease.

nodes.name: RDD Asymptomatic Treatment
nodes.title: RDD, Asymptomatic or Mild Nodal: Active Surveillance
nodes.description: Asymptomatic or mild nodal RDD without compressive or extranodal progressive disease. Active surveillance is the standard.
bullets: Active surveillance: observation without systemic therapy; a substantial fraction of nodal RDD remains stable or regresses spontaneously.
Follow-up: serial clinical examination with nodal measurement, symptom review, and periodic imaging (ultrasound, CT, or FDG PET-CT) for progressive or extranodal evolution.
Intervention triggers: compressive symptoms, airway or orbital compromise, CNS involvement, cytopenias, or progressive extranodal disease prompts re-triage to the symptomatic pathway.
Counseling: reassure on the generally indolent course of isolated nodal disease while documenting baseline extent for comparison.

nodes.name: RDD Symptomatic Treatment
nodes.title: RDD, Symptomatic or Extranodal: Systemic Therapy
nodes.description: Symptomatic nodal or extranodal RDD (skin, orbit, CNS, airway). Corticosteroid backbone with MEK inhibition for systemic or refractory disease; surgery for compressive lesions.
bullets: First-line systemic: corticosteroids for symptomatic nodal or extranodal RDD, tapered to response with gastric, glycemic, and bone protection.
Systemic or refractory disease: cobimetinib (Category 1 preferred for systemic refractory RDD), with dose engine calculating patient-specific doses; confirm MAPK pathway status on broad NGS.
Alternative systemic: cladribine for steroid-refractory or multiply relapsed RDD.

Compressive lesions: surgical debulking or excision for airway, orbital, spinal, or CNS compression in parallel with systemic therapy planning; radiotherapy reserved for selected unresectable critical-site disease.

nodes.name: Malignant Localized Treatment
nodes.title: Malignant Histiocytosis, Resectable Localized: Surgery With or Without RT
nodes.description: Resectable localized histiocytic sarcoma without distant spread. Wide surgical excision with or without adjuvant radiotherapy.
bullets: Wide surgical excision with clear margins as the curative-intent backbone for solitary resectable disease.
Adjuvant radiotherapy for close or positive margins, high-grade features, or sites where re-excision is morbid; dose and field per soft-tissue sarcoma principles.
Staging confirmation: whole-body FDG PET-CT and bone marrow assessment to exclude occult systemic spread before committing to a local-only plan.
Surveillance: intensive clinical and imaging follow-up because distant relapse risk is high even after complete resection; re-biopsy and NGS at any recurrence.

nodes.name: Malignant Advanced Treatment
nodes.title: Malignant Histiocytosis, Advanced or Systemic: Anthracycline-Based Chemotherapy
nodes.description: Advanced or systemic histiocytic sarcoma. Anthracycline-based chemotherapy (CHOP or ifosfamide-based) with conditional targeted therapy when a kinase alteration is identified.
bullets: Backbone: anthracycline-based chemotherapy with CHOP, or an ifosfamide-based regimen for fit patients with aggressive systemic disease; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

Conditional targeted therapy: add or switch to BRAF-directed therapy for BRAF V600E, MEK inhibition for MAPK pathway alteration, or ALK-directed therapy for ALK fusion identified on comprehensive NGS.
Baseline and on-treatment: cardiac function (anthracycline), CBC/renal/hepatic panels, fertility counseling, growth-factor support per febrile-neutropenia risk.
Restaging: FDG PET-CT after 2 to 3 cycles to judge chemosensitivity; early progression prompts regimen switch, targeted pivot on new molecular result, or clinical trial referral.
